If a reserved seat has remained unpaid for more than 30 minutes, the system must release that seat. [in logic: (and seat_reserved (> seat_unpaid_minutes 30)) => seat_released]
situation: The seat has not been released, no seat has been reserved for the passenger, and the number of minutes a reserved seat has been unpaid is 31.
title: Ambiguity in seat release condition
explanation: Requirement F4 is ambiguous because it is unclear whether the system should release a seat based solely on the time elapsed since payment was due, or if the seat must also currently be in a reserved state. In the situation described, the seat is not reserved and has not been released, yet the unpaid time is 31 minutes. Under the first reading, the system would be required to release the seat because the time limit was exceeded, whereas under the second reading, the system would not release the seat because it is not currently reserved. Which did you mean?
option_a: Keep the requirement as written, meaning the system releases a seat whenever the unpaid time exceeds 30 minutes, regardless of whether the seat is currently marked as reserved.
option_b: Reword the requirement to explicitly state that the system shall release the seat only if the seat is currently reserved and has been unpaid for more than 30 minutes.

If a vehicle space has been released and the booked vehicle has not checked in, the system must have released the vehicle space. [in logic: (and vehicle_space_released (not vehicle_checked_in) (= minutes_before_departure 30)) => true]
situation: The number of minutes before departure is 30, the booked vehicle has not checked in, and a vehicle space has not been released.
title: Ambiguous vehicle release timing
explanation: Requirement F21 can be read in two different ways. The first reading says that if a vehicle has not checked in 30 minutes before departure, the system must release its vehicle space. The second reading says that if a vehicle space has been released and the vehicle has not checked in exactly 30 minutes before departure, the system must have released the space. Which did you mean?
option_a: Keep the requirement as written, meaning the system must release the vehicle space if the vehicle has not checked in 30 minutes before departure.
option_b: Rewrite the requirement to state that the system must release the vehicle space if the vehicle has not checked in 30 minutes before departure, removing the alternative interpretation.

situation: A passenger has asked for a printed ticket at the port office.
title: Ticket Printing Contradiction
explanation: The requirements contain a direct conflict regarding the printing of tickets. Requirement F9 states that the system must print a ticket when a passenger asks for one at the port office, while Requirement F101 states that the system must never print tickets. In the situation where a passenger asks for a printed ticket, the system is forced to both print the ticket and not print the ticket, which is impossible.
option_a: Keeping the requirements as written means the system is in a state of logical contradiction and cannot function correctly when a passenger requests a printed ticket.
option_b: Remove Requirement F9 or modify it to state that the system shall provide a digital alternative or direct the passenger to a self-service kiosk, thereby removing the obligation to print tickets that conflicts with Requirement F101.

situation: A group booking has been paid, and the number of passengers in the group booking is 10.
title: Group discount threshold ambiguity
explanation: The requirements do not specify what the system must do when a group booking of exactly 10 passengers is paid. Requirement F11 states that a group discount is applied when a group booking of more than 10 passengers is paid, which implies that a group of exactly 10 passengers does not qualify for the discount. However, the term "group booking" is not explicitly defined by a minimum passenger count elsewhere, leaving it unclear if a booking of 10 is considered a group for other purposes or if the discount threshold is intended to be inclusive of 10.
option_a: Keeping the requirements as written means that a group booking of exactly 10 passengers will not receive the 10 percent group discount, as the condition "more than 10" is not met.
option_b: Change requirement F11 to state that the group discount is applied when a group booking of 10 or more passengers is paid.

situation: The gate has been opened, but no passenger has scanned an e-ticket at the gate, and the ticket is not valid for the next sailing.
title: Gate opens without valid scan
explanation: Requirement F26 states that the gate shall open only when a passenger scans an e-ticket that is valid for the next sailing. The proven behaviour shows the gate opening in a situation where neither a scan occurred nor was the ticket valid, which directly contradicts the security and access control purpose of the requirement. This allows unauthorized boarding, which is clearly against the goal of managing passenger access safely.
option_a: Keep the requirements, so the behaviour stays allowed.
option_b: Modify Requirement F26 to explicitly state that the gate shall remain closed unless a valid e-ticket scan for the next sailing is detected.

situation: The cabin door has been unlocked, the entered door code is not correct, and a passenger has not entered a door code at the cabin.
title: Cabin door unlocked without code entry
explanation: The requirements state that a cabin door is only unlocked when a passenger enters the correct door code (F37). However, the system allows the door to be unlocked even when no passenger has entered a code and the code is not correct. This defeats the purpose of the door code security measure, as it allows unauthorized access to the cabin.
option_a: Keep the requirements, so the behaviour stays allowed.
option_b: Add a requirement that the cabin door SHALL remain locked unless a passenger enters the correct door code.

situation: A passenger has not added a pet to a booking, yet the pet fee has been added to the fare.
title: Pet fee charged without pet
explanation: Requirement F68 states that the pet fee is added to the fare when a passenger adds a pet to a booking. The logic solver proved that the requirements allow the pet fee to be added to the fare even when no pet has been added to the booking. This is clearly against the goal of the requirement, which is to charge the fee only when a pet is actually part of the booking.
option_a: Keep the requirements, so the behaviour of adding a pet fee without a pet remains allowed.
option_b: Change requirement F68 to explicitly state that the pet fee SHALL NOT be added to the fare unless a pet has been added to the booking.
